en.title: How to evaluate foundation performance
en.subtitle: Four different failures wearing one name
en.excerpt: Wear time is four separate things wearing one name. Here is how to tell them apart before you blame the wrong one.
en.openingParagraph: When a foundation fails, almost everyone reaches the same conclusion: it does not last. But four completely different things get described that way, and they have different causes and different fixes. Separating them is the single most useful skill in complexion testing, because three of the four are solvable and one is not.

sections.heading: Breakdown is not the same as transfer
sections.summary: Product leaving the face versus product moving on the face. Different causes, different fixes.

sections.heading: Colour shift, and how to actually check for it
sections.summary: Photograph at hour zero in fixed lighting or you cannot make this claim at all.

sections.heading: Separation and where it starts
sections.summary: It nearly always begins in the same three places, and where it begins tells you what caused it.

sections.heading: Finish change over time
sections.summary: A satin base going shiny at hour four may be doing exactly what it should. Know the difference.

sections.heading: Why conditions matter more than the formula
sections.summary: The same base can pass at 22 degrees and fail at 36. A review that omits conditions is not reporting a result.

sections.heading: A test you can run at home
sections.summary: Three photographs, one napkin, fixed lighting, four check-ins.

seo.title: How to evaluate foundation performance
seo.description: Breakdown, transfer, colour shift and finish change are four different failures. How to tell them apart and run a fair wear test at home.

ar.openingParagraph: حين يفشل كريم الأساس، تصل معظمنا إلى النتيجة نفسها: إنه لا يثبت. لكن أربعة أمور مختلفة تماما تُوصف بهذه الطريقة، ولكل منها سبب مختلف وحل مختلف. الفصل بينها هو أنفع مهارة في اختبار منتجات البشرة، لأن ثلاثة من الأربعة قابلة للحل وواحدا ليس كذلك.

en.title: What makes a beauty review useful
en.subtitle: You should be able to disagree with it
en.excerpt: A review is useful when you can reconstruct the reasoning and decide it was wrong. Most reviews make that impossible.
en.openingParagraph: The test of a good review is not whether you agree with the verdict. It is whether you can see how the verdict was reached clearly enough to disagree with it. If a review tells you a foundation is amazing and nothing else, there is nothing to argue with, and nothing to use.

ar.openingParagraph: معيار المراجعة الجيدة ليس اتفاقك مع الحكم، بل قدرتك على رؤية كيف وُصل إلى الحكم بوضوح يكفي للاختلاف معه. إذا أخبرتك مراجعة أن كريم الأساس رائع ولا شيء غير ذلك، فلا يوجد ما يمكن مناقشته، ولا ما يمكن استخدامه.

en.title: Understanding finish and texture
en.subtitle: Six words, no shared definitions
en.excerpt: Matte, satin, natural, luminous, radiant, dewy. Six words, no shared definitions, and one reason you keep buying the wrong base.
en.openingParagraph: There is no industry standard for what a finish name means. One brand's natural is another brand's matte, and radiant and luminous are used interchangeably by companies that mean very different things by them. This is not a conspiracy; it is just an unregulated vocabulary. But it means you cannot shop by finish name alone, and it explains a surprising share of disappointing purchases.

en.title: Building a practical routine
en.subtitle: Design it for your worst morning
en.excerpt: The best routine is the one you can repeat on a bad day. A method for building one, and for finding which step is causing the problem.
en.openingParagraph: Routines fail for boring reasons. They take too long on the mornings that matter, they contain a step nobody enjoys, or they change so often that nothing can be attributed to anything. A routine you can repeat for four weeks without thinking about it is worth more than a better routine you abandon in nine days.

en.title: How to compare beauty products fairly
en.subtitle: Two products, one face, one day
en.excerpt: Almost every comparison you have read broke at least one of these rules.
en.openingParagraph: A comparison is only a comparison if one variable changed. Two foundations tested on different days, in different weather, over different skincare, applied with different tools, are not being compared. They are being described in sequence and then ranked, which is a different and much less useful thing.

ar.title: مفردات درجات البشرة: لماذا لا تُترجم
ar.subtitle: الدرجة التي تشترينها ليست الدرجة التي تصفينها
ar.excerpt: مصطلحات الدرجات في العربية لا تقابل مصطلحات العلامات الأجنبية. هذا الدليل يفكك المسافة بينهما.
ar.openingParagraph: حين تصف إحدانا بشرتها بأنها قمحية، لا يوجد رقم يقابل ذلك على أي عبوة. وحين تكتب علامة أجنبية warm sand أو golden beige، فهي تصف نظاما داخليا لا يشبه بالضرورة ما نعنيه. هذه ليست مشكلة لغة، بل مشكلة نظامين للتصنيف نشآ في مكانين مختلفين ولأغراض مختلفة، ونحن نتسوق في المسافة بينهما.
